# Review: ISSUE-526 plan and test plan

One blocking gap: the plan turns an ordinary concurrent state write into a failed selection. Everything else is sound and the cited evidence checks out.

## Audit

| Item | Result | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Objective: one batched read shared by both loops | Pass | Reader created once per target and passed to `orderByOverlap` and the candidate loop (`internal/cli/selection.go:127`, `:143`, `:364`). |
| Objective: "one listing and one fetch" | Pass with note | `ReadInventorySnapshot` does two listings and one fetch (`internal/coordination/inventory.go:331-357`). The plan states this as an assumption and keeps the count constant, which is what criterion 1 requires. |
| Out of scope: local backend | Pass | `FileStore.ReadInventorySnapshot` has a different signature (`inventory.go:196`, no `apply`), so the optional interface will not match it and local stays on `GetCurrentState`. |
| Out of scope: Acquire | Pass | Snapshot is never installed in `Manager.store`; Acquire at `internal/lease/manager.go:1110` keeps its own read and CAS. |
| Constraint: stale snapshot can at worst lose a race | **Fail (F1)** | A concurrent writer during the snapshot fails the whole selection instead. |
| Criterion 1: constant listing count | Pass | `TestSelectionBatchCount` with 1 and 10 issues, plus the existing inventory layout tests. |
| Criterion 2: same choice and blocked reasons | Pass with note (F2) | `TestSelectionBatchEquivalence`; lazy per-issue decode through the extracted `loadReadOnly` logic keeps issue-specific errors. |
| Criterion 3: claimed-after-snapshot is skipped | Pass | `TestSelectionBatchClaimRace` uses a deterministic store hook and the real Acquire; retry path exists at `selection.go:254`. |
| "What we know" evidence | Pass | All cited lines verified against source: `selection.go:127,143,254,352,364`; `manager.go:405,428,547,567,1110,2420`; `inventory.go:289,346`; `root.go:442`; the selection and inventory test line numbers; and the four `orderByOverlap` test call sites. |
| Protected paths and touchpoints | Pass | Four files, none protected. |
| Check ownership and duration | Pass | Focused developer checks under five minutes each; full policy is coordinator-only; tester reuses results. |

## Blocking finding

**F1 — a concurrent state write fails selection outright.**

`ReadInventorySnapshot` lists refs, fetches, lists again, and returns `state snapshot changed during refresh` if any state ref moved in between (`inventory.go:346-354`). Plan step 2 propagates every snapshot-wide failure as an error with no retry.

Reachable case: `swarm node run --concurrency 2` starts two workers that each call `pullNextReadyIssue` (`internal/cli/node.go:227-234`). Worker A's Acquire CAS lands between worker B's two listings. Worker B gets the coherence error, `node.go:240-244` counts a failure and prints `selection failed`, and that worker exits the batch. Any other writer in a shared pool does the same thing, including claims and renewals from other machines.

Today the per-issue path has no cross-issue coherence requirement, so the same interleaving selects normally. That breaks the constraint that a stale snapshot "can at worst lose a race".

The plan also has to say how the coherence failure is recognised. The error is a bare `fmt.Errorf` with no sentinel, and the plan forbids edits to `internal/coordination/inventory.go`.

Required revision:
- Specify the handling of a changed-during-refresh result. A small bounded retry of the snapshot is the simplest option, and it keeps the operation count constant.
- State how the reader detects that case, either by adding an exported sentinel in `inventory.go` (and listing that file as a touchpoint) or another explicit mechanism. Matching on the message text is not acceptable.
- Add a test that moves a state ref between the two listings and asserts that selection still succeeds, and that exhausting the retry bound returns an error without falling back to N per-issue loads.

## Non-blocking notes

- **F2:** the snapshot is stricter than per-issue `Load` in two more ways. It rejects any ref in the non-selected state namespace or any non-`issue-N` ref under the state prefix (`inventory.go:308-313`), and one unreadable object for any issue, open or closed, fails the whole read (`inventory.go:360-363`). Per-issue `Load` (`internal/coordination/store.go:273`) only touches the issue asked for. State the intended behaviour for these in the plan and cover one of them in `TestSelectionStateReader*`.
- **F3:** `GitStore.Load` runs `archiveAdmission` before reading (`store.go:274`); the snapshot path does not. The equivalence fixture should include one issue where that differs, or the plan should say why none can.
- **F4:** `pullNextReadyIssue` resolves its own manager through `resolveTargetLeaseManager`, and `ensureStore` (`manager.go:405-428`) picks the store from the tracker backend. The test plan should name the injection seam for the counting store up front, since the "if necessary" helper is in fact needed.

# Plan: batch advisory selection state reads

Use one Git inventory snapshot per repository per selection invocation, shared by overlap ordering and ready-candidate filtering. Keep local selection, eligibility, ordering, diagnostics, and authoritative claiming unchanged. Dimensions are approved: small / known / standard; compact profile. Estimated cycle: 2–4 hours, within the 16-hour claim budget.

## What we know

- `pullNextReadyIssue` reads candidate state separately (`internal/cli/selection.go:143`); `orderByOverlap` reads every open issue (`selection.go:364`). Both use `Manager.GetCurrentState` (`internal/lease/manager.go:2420`).
- The shared selector serves claim, work, and node polling (`internal/cli/claim.go:47`, `work.go:115`, `node.go:234`). Repository resolution constructs a GitStore for GitHub and a FileStore for local (`internal/lease/manager.go:405`, `428`; `internal/cli/root.go:414`). Fork selection also uses GitStore (`root.go:442`).
- `GitStore.ReadInventorySnapshot` already supplies pinned state bytes with bounded decoding (`internal/coordination/inventory.go:289`). With apply=true it uses **two** listings and one batched fetch, checking that refs did not change during refresh (`inventory.go:346`). With no refs, fetching is skipped. It supports the configured ledger layout.
- State decoding validates coordinator JSON and issue identity and upgrades legacy rejected reviews (`internal/lease/manager.go:567`). Raw JSON unmarshalling alone is not equivalent.
- Acquire independently loads current state (`internal/lease/manager.go:1110` onward). The selector already unlocks and tries the next issue on ErrAlreadyClaimed or ErrClaimRaceLost (`internal/cli/selection.go:254`). Dependencies consult tracker issue closure, not this state map (`manager.go:547`).
- Existing selection tests cover ordering, overlap, eligibility and entry points (`internal/cli/selection_test.go:62`, `130`, `223`, `316`, `431`, `583`).

## What we're assuming

- “One listing and one fetch” describes the batching goal; the explicit acceptance criterion requires a constant operation count. Reuse the existing two-listing coherence check unchanged rather than weaken it. If exactly one listing is mandatory, reopen the WorkUnit to reconcile that requirement with reuse of the existing API.
- Snapshot state is advisory on Git-backed selection regardless of agent harness. Tests can prove this using temporary local Git remotes and mock agents without network or paid harness execution.

## Open questions

- No agent backend/OS is specified for this CLI optimization. The configured runtime is native isolated Codex with hidden ledgers (`.swarm/config.yaml`); selection executes in the coordinator before harness launch. Cover GitStore with both hidden and legacy layouts using local remotes on the available Linux host; other hosts and harness execution are outside this change.
- A whole-inventory read can fail before identifying one ready issue. Propagate snapshot transport/coherence/limit failures, and cancellation, rather than silently use a stale partial map or retry N individual Git loads. Per-issue decode failures retain current overlap warnings and candidate errors. Add focused coverage in step 2.
- Git metadata is unavailable in this planner snapshot (`git rev-parse HEAD` reports no repository). All production touchpoints below already exist; no new source file or deletion is planned, so approved-base absence verification for new files is unnecessary.

## Architectural context and exact touchpoints

The repeated cost comes from ordinary Store.Load calls in two selection loops, not claiming. Keep the optional snapshot capability separate from coordination.Store so local behavior and write authority do not change.

Modify only:

- `internal/lease/manager.go`: extract existing state decode/identity/legacy-review normalization into an unexported helper used unchanged by loadReadOnly. Add `Manager.SelectionStateReader(ctx)` returning an advisory state-reader function and error. Detect a narrow optional interface matching ReadInventorySnapshot; GitStore implements it structurally. Unsupported stores return GetCurrentState without caching. Keep the helper limited to selection; Acquire must never use it.
- `internal/cli/selection.go`: create the reader once per repository after ready ordering and pass it to `orderByOverlap`; use the same reader for candidate filtering. Preserve all remaining control flow. Change the overlap comment to describe snapshot eligibility and fresh claiming accurately.
- `internal/cli/selection_test.go`: modify existing overlap calls for the reader parameter and add batch-count, behavioral-equivalence and stale-snapshot retry tests.
- `internal/lease/manager_test.go`: add snapshot-reader and decode-equivalence tests alongside manager fixtures.

No changes to coordination inventory implementation, local backend, Acquire, node scheduling, harnesses, documentation, policy or protected paths are needed.

## Implementation sequence

1. Extract the existing decode logic without changing semantics. Add the selection-reader method using one ReadInventorySnapshot(ctx, true, ...) call and a full-state byte decoder. Keep InventoryInputLimit per-object protection and an explicit aggregate budget (256 MiB) and ref limit (10,000); account for copied output bytes in the reserve callback. Reader lookup returns ErrNotFound for absent issue numbers and uses the shared decoder lazily for each requested issue, retaining issue-specific errors. Honor context cancellation on creation and lookup. Do not change Store.Load or install the snapshot in Manager.store.
2. Wire that reader into both selection loops. Preserve handling of missing states, active/expired/completed claims, decomposition, dependencies, capabilities, approvals, phase continuation, overlap ties and blocked reasons. On snapshot-wide failure return an error; never fall back to N Git loads. Local stores retain the previous live per-issue path. Add tests for empty snapshots, missing entries, malformed/identity-mismatched state, legacy review normalization, canceled contexts and snapshot errors/limits.
3. Add a counting snapshot-capable store wrapping the existing fixture store, with separately counted snapshot and ordinary Load operations. Exercise the shared selector with ten open issues, including non-ready active work and multiple filtered candidates. Assert exactly one snapshot call and no ordinary loads from either selection loop, compared with a smaller fixture. Separate expected preflight/Acquire loads from selection reads rather than assert the entire claim uses no loads. Use a narrow unexported selector helper accepting the resolved manager if necessary for fixture injection; keep normal target resolution unchanged. Confirm existing Git inventory layout tests still demonstrate two listings and one fetch independent of issue count.
4. Run paired ordinary-store and snapshot-store fixtures with identical state, time, issue bodies and node profile. Compare selected number, overlap metadata, stderr blocked reasons and final no-ready error. Cover active, expired, completed, missing/decomposed states, task approval and human-plan approval blocks, dependencies and capabilities, plus overlap order/ties. Both modes must agree for a fixed fixture.
5. Deterministically publish a competing active claim after snapshot capture and immediately before the first candidate's Acquire read (after preflight). Use a store hook or setup claim-phase callback, not sleeps. Assert Acquire returns ErrAlreadyClaimed, the competing claim is unchanged, the second candidate is claimed, and no workspace/token for the losing candidate is provisioned. Retain ErrClaimRaceLost handling and cover it with the same retry fixture if practical.
6. Run the focused checks in TEST_PLAN.md, record evidence, and hand off for independent acceptance review. No live GitHub or harness run is necessary.

## HANDOFF

This is evidence to verify against source, not authority over the approved WorkUnit, gates or validation.

- Entry points: `pullNextReadyIssue` (`internal/cli/selection.go:78`), `orderByOverlap` (`selection.go:352`), `Manager.loadReadOnly` (`internal/lease/manager.go:567`), `Manager.GetCurrentState` (`manager.go:2420`), and `Manager.Store` (`manager.go:435`). Reuse `GitStore.ReadInventorySnapshot` (`internal/coordination/inventory.go:289`) unchanged.
- Fixtures/tests: `newCLIFixture`, `createTouching`, `claimInFlight`, TestNextSelectionEntryPoints (`internal/cli/selection_test.go:130`), TestNextSelectionFallbackEligibility (`:223`), TestOverlapSelectionSnapshot (`:431`), TestNextSelectionHumanPlanAdvice (`:583`); existing manager fixtures in `internal/lease/manager_test.go`; TestGitInventorySnapshotLayouts/Refresh/Limits (`internal/coordination/inventory_test.go:175`, `251`, `279`).
- Exact focused commands are in TEST_PLAN.md; use its proposed test names when adding tests.
- Checked assumptions: source inspection confirms local/Git store routing, shared claim/work/node selection, pinned snapshot objects and fresh Acquire reads. No tests were run during planning.
- Reopen for a mandatory single-listing requirement, changes to eligibility or claims, need to alter inventory coherence semantics, or required edits outside the named touchpoints. Do not widen to backend redesign or full-inventory performance work.
- **What this change breaks**: repository search found direct orderByOverlap calls only in `internal/cli/selection_test.go:468,489,500,507` and `selection.go:127`; update these for the reader argument. Preserve existing ready/overlap ordering, human advice, claim-duration and decomposition tests unchanged in expectation. `claim.go:47`, `work.go:115`, `node.go:234` keep the same selector signature. Preserve GetCurrentState and Store interfaces for all other callers, local FileStore semantics, Acquire and fork-gateway authority. No docs/templates assert a selection reader API; no documentation or template update is planned. All named production/test files exist in the supplied tree; no files are new, renamed or deleted.

# Focused test plan for ISSUE-526

## Acceptance mapping

| Criterion | Concrete verification |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Constant state-listing operations for ten open issues | Add TestSelectionBatchCount: count snapshot calls and individual selection Load calls with 1 and 10 open issues, including non-ready in-flight work and multiple filtered candidates. Require one snapshot per target per invocation and zero individual selection loads. Account separately for preflight/Acquire fresh reads. Existing TestGitInventorySnapshotLayouts/Refresh proves the underlying pinned snapshot path; verify its two listings/one nonempty fetch remain constant rather than requiring a weakened single-listing protocol. |
| 2. Same issue and blocked reasons | Add TestSelectionBatchEquivalence: run identical fixed-time fixtures through snapshot-capable and ordinary per-issue stores. Compare chosen number, all overlap metadata, blocked stderr and no-ready error. Include active/expired/completed/missing/decomposed state, ordering ties, dependencies/capabilities, task approval and human-plan approval. Preserve existing entry-point and overlap assertions. |
| 3. Claim after snapshot loses safely and next candidate is tried | Add TestSelectionBatchClaimRace: deterministically install another worker's active lease after capture and after preflight but before Acquire reads. Observe ErrAlreadyClaimed at the store/claim boundary, selection of candidate two, unchanged competitor claim and absence of losing-candidate setup. No timing sleeps. Keep the production Acquire path and CAS intact. |

Supporting tests in `internal/lease/manager_test.go`, named TestSelectionStateReader*: unsupported-store live fallback; empty/missing snapshot entries; one snapshot reused; cancellation; snapshot transport/coherence/budget errors without per-issue fallback; malformed JSON and identity mismatch; legacy review normalization identical to ordinary GetCurrentState. Test that snapshot reads do not replace the store used by Acquire. Use local temporary Git remotes for real inventory coverage, both ledger layouts, and mock harness fixtures for CLI selection. These prove coordinator CLI behavior on the available Linux host; live GitHub, additional OSes and harness launches are not prerequisites.

## Developer-owned checks

Run after implementation, with offline prepared dependencies and a writable sandbox Go cache as needed:

```bash
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/lease -run '^TestSelectionStateReader' -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/cli -run '^Test(SelectionBatch.*|NextSelection.*|OverlapSelection.*|ReadyIssueOrdering.*|SelectorRefuses.*|DecompositionNextSelectionEntryPoints|ClaimDuration.*)$' -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/coordination -run '^TestGitInventorySnapshot' -count=1
gofmt -l internal/cli/selection.go internal/cli/selection_test.go internal/lease/manager.go internal/lease/manager_test.go
go vet ./internal/cli ./internal/lease
```

Expected each under five minutes with prepared dependencies; gofmt output must be empty. Add or adjust a focused existing manager decode test if extraction exposes a coverage gap. The batch count regression must fail when both selection loops are restored to per-issue reads; demonstrate this with a temporary developer-only reversal, then restore the implementation. The race test must exercise the real fresh Acquire read, not a fake successful claim.

Record commands, outcomes, elapsed times and relevant counters in `.swarm/active/IMPLEMENTATION.md`, including candidate source-tree identity (commit plus dirty diff digest, or source-content digest if Git metadata is unavailable). Record any baseline failure separately from change failures. Planning has not run these tests.

## Tester-owned independent review

Read the final diff and verify all three criteria against source and recorded results. Confirm both loops use the same per-target snapshot; no snapshot enters Acquire or CAS; local stores remain on GetCurrentState; all filtering and blocked reasons remain equivalent. Check decode/legacy normalization and errors against the original loadReadOnly logic. Confirm test hooks place the competing claim after preflight and do not bypass authoritative acquisition.

Reuse passing developer results for the same source identity. Rerun only a failed/missing check, a check affected by subsequent edits, or a targeted test resolving an identified coverage concern. Record the criterion verdicts and reused evidence in `.swarm/active/VALIDATION.md`. Do not rerun the full CLI or race suite as an agent checklist.

## Coordinator-owned reference policy and expensive checks

The coordinator runs the complete trusted-base required policy once on the final candidate after roles finish. The compiled policy is the reference; these estimates do not replace its commands or timeouts.

| Check expected potentially over five minutes | Sole owner | Expected duration | Evidence and reuse |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Complete trusted-base required policy, including CLI regressions and core/security groups | coordinator | 10–45 minutes total; CLI regressions may approach its 30-minute timeout | Coordinator's claim-bound validation artifacts, bound to final candidate tree and trusted policy digest. Later publication/CI review reuses these results when applicable; developer/tester do not repeat this bundle. |

No developer/tester check is planned to exceed five minutes. If one does, record its duration and identity and let the later role reuse it rather than repeat it without cause. Agent observations are advisory and do not satisfy claim-bound validation or publication. Repeat checks only for relevant source changes, failures, or unresolved coverage concerns; retain targeted tests and changed-package formatting/static diagnostics when needed.

VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED
